title: Gideon and the Oath
premise: Ada Reyes, a cartographer of unmapped realms, has spent his life charting the valley where magic cannot follow — the one place the old gods' war never reached. When the gods begin answering prayers again, a dying messenger presses a sealed oath into his hands: proof that the valley's peace was built on a stolen name and a buried crime. Hunted by both divine factions who want the secret destroyed or weaponized, Ada must cross into realms he has only ever drawn from rumor. In the end, he chooses neither side: he rewrites the oath itself, unbinding the gods from their ancient claim and giving the stolen name back to its true heirs — at the cost of his own place in any map ever made.
about_author: Silas Brightwater is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to coastlines that do not exist. They write fantasy about people caught between what they inherit and what they choose.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Establishes Ada's meticulous life mapping the unmappable valley and his quiet hunger to leave. He finishes a map no one asked for and burns the edges where his hand strayed beyond known borders. Emotional beat: restless contentment about to crack.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered Wrong
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The village shrine, silent for generations, answers a child's prayer with a voice like grinding stone. Ada witnesses it and realizes magic has crossed the boundary that defined his whole world. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Dying Messenger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A bloodied stranger stumbles into Ada's workshop carrying a sealed oath-scroll, whispering 'the name was taken' before dying. Soldiers of both god-factions arrive searching for it; Ada hides the scroll inside a rolled map. Emotional beat: fear fused with complicity.

chapters.title: What the Oath Says
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, alone at night. He breaks the seal and reads the oath: the valley's peace was purchased with a god's stolen true name, held in trust by a mortal line — possibly his own. Emotional beat: vertigo of inheritance; his identity becomes a question.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Maren's POV introduced — a sharp-eyed courier for the god Vessan's faction who suspects her employers lie. She traces the messenger's route to the valley. Emotional beat: professional loyalty beginning to fray.

chapters.title: Leaving the Map
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. With soldiers closing in, Ada flees the valley through a pass he mapped only from hearsay, crossing the boundary where magic floods back into him like cold water. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of finally leaving home.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Traveling through countryside where minor gods answer every prayer, Ada learns the old war ended not in victory but in exhaustion — and that the stolen name is the truce's keystone. Emotional beat: the weight of being a carrier, not an owner.

chapters.title: Maren Catches Up
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She corners Ada at a river ferry, intending arrest, but his knowledge of the oath unsettles her — Vessan told her the scroll was heresy, not history. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of shared doubt.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Lake
chapters.summary: Shared POV alternating. Maren leads Ada to a drowned archive where oaths are stored; they find the original covenant naming the thief of the god's name — a revered founder, and an ancestor of Ada's line. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as guilt.

chapters.title: Vessan Descends
chapters.summary: Vessan's POV. The god interrogates Maren's failure and reveals his plan: use the oath to prove his right to the stolen name and restart the war on favorable terms. Emotional beat: chilling certainty; the antagonist believes himself just.

chapters.title: The Other Faction
chapters.summary: Ada and Maren's POV. Captured by the rival faction, the Ashen Choir, who want the name destroyed so no god can ever wield it. Their leader offers Ada sanctuary if he surrenders the scroll. Emotional beat: temptation of safety through erasure.

chapters.title: A Name of One's Own
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Imprisoned, Ada confronts what his family's theft means: everything he is stands on a crime. He begins drafting, in cartographer's habit, a third option — redrawing the oath rather than delivering or destroying it. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt as authorship.

chapters.title: Maren's Choice
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Ordered to retrieve the scroll and kill Ada, she instead frees him, burning her standing with Vessan forever. Emotional beat: justice chosen over obedience, at real cost.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Burnt Country
chapters.summary: Shared POV. A desperate journey across a battlefield-landscape still scarred by the old war, where dead prayers still echo. They outrun both factions toward the neutral conclave at Greyford. Emotional beat: two fugitives becoming true partners.

chapters.title: The Conclave of Greyford
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Mortal arbiters hear Ada's evidence but fear both gods; they offer to bury the oath and preserve the fragile peace. Ada must decide whether peace built on theft deserves preserving. Emotional beat: the law failing where conscience must act.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. A conclave clerk sells them out; Vessan's forces breach Greyford. In the chaos the scroll is seized — but Ada has already memorized and altered its terms in a hidden draft. Emotional beat: loss that conceals a gambit.

chapters.title: The Trial of Names
chapters.summary: Vessan's POV. Before both factions, Vessan demands the stolen name be restored to him by right. The Ashen Choir demands annihilation of the name. The conclave turns to Ada as the heir who holds the trust. Emotional beat: courtroom tension; all eyes on the least powerful person present.

chapters.title: What Ada Rewrote
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada presents his amended oath: the name belongs to no god but returns to the mortals who suffered the war, severing divine claim entirely. Both factions rage; the assembled mortals, hearing their own names invoked, rise in support. Emotional beat: quiet courage igniting collective will.

chapters.title: The War That Almost Was
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vessan attacks; the Choir counters; the sky tears open above Greyford. Ada and Maren race to inscribe the new oath onto the covenant stone mid-battle. Emotional beat: climax — ink and blood, the fate of realms in a few lines of text.

chapters.title: Signing
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada completes the inscription as Vessan bears down on him; the amended oath takes hold, unbinding the stolen name and stripping the gods' warrant for war. Vessan falters, diminished but not destroyed, and withdraws. Emotional beat: triumph laced with grief.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Man
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Aftermath: the gods recede into silence, the valley boundary dissolves, and Ada — having given his family's claim away — finds himself legally and magically no one. Maren offers him a place on the road. Emotional beat: freedom found in dispossession.

chapters.title: Blank Margins
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue. Years later, Ada and Maren map the newly reachable realms together, leaving deliberate blank spaces as gifts to future travelers. He keeps the original oath's first line framed: 'the name was taken.' Emotional beat: peace as an ongoing act of drawing, not a finished map.
